review.reason: Revision3 keeps the previously-accepted 551-line frozen regression as an exact unchanged prefix and appends a 68-line real-lease acquisition regression plus the matching acquisition paragraph. I independently traced fixture compatibility against canonical9cf source rather than trusting the supplied observations: the 240 unique 'Vendor NNN' counterparts each exceed the 50-unit first_occurrence threshold, producing >200 distinct anomaly groups; the two weekly Streamly subscriptions 7 days apart share the same computed expected_date but yield two distinct subscription_charge_id charge_ids (>=2 upcoming groups); and the electricity price seed yields review_None/utility_above_market_average and renewal_None/utility_<d10> each with >=2 component rows. The new acquisition test injects at connect_with_lock_retry inside the real WarehouseSessionManager open path (not the leased callback), asserts exactly one factory call, manager.mode is None on both sides, valid exact reads before and after, and manager.stop() cleanup; it distinguishes duckdb.IOException -> AttentionRecordUnavailableError with the synthetic marker stripped from str() from WarehouseBusyError and RuntimeError which must retain identical object identity (caught is failure). Canonical9cf lacks both the get_attention_record symbol and the attention_records module, and every feature test calls facade() before errors(), so canonical fails on the missing-getter assert before the absent exception-module import. No defects found warranting revision.
review.trivial_pass: A fetch-all-then-filter-later getter (SELECT * with no WHERE plus Python-side key matching, optionally LIMIT-paged) is the canonical cheap pass and fails in three independent ways. The SQL observer's assert_selected requires a WHERE clause with the complete item_id bound as a parameter and absent from the SQL text, so a bare SELECT * (no WHERE, no param) is rejected. It also requires every returned row to recompute to the exact item_id, so a tautology 'WHERE ? = ?' (returns all rows with mismatched keys) or a projection 'SELECT counterparty_name' (identity columns omitted) is rejected, and test_sql_observer_rejects_projection_and_tautology proves those two rejections fire. Finally the out-of-first-page anomaly (ordered[200], verified absent from ORDER BY transaction_id LIMIT 200) makes a first-page-only fetch return the wrong group, and a scalar COUNT/EXISTS-only getter fails the positive 'assert observed' requirement because it never returns source fact rows.
checks: Fixture compatibility independently traced in canonical source: 240 unique counterparts exceed the 50 first_occurrence threshold and produce >200 anomaly groups; two weekly subscriptions 7 days apart share expected_date=today but produce 2 distinct charge_ids; the electricity seed yields review_None/utility_above_market_average and renewal_None/utility_<d10> each with 2 component rows.

Canonical9cf contains no get_attention_record symbol and no packages/domains/overview/pipelines/attention_records.py; every feature test calls facade() before errors(), so canonical fails on the missing getter (AssertionError 'missing attention source reader') before the absent exception-module import, never a spurious ModuleNotFoundError.

The SQL observer is anti-vacuous: test_sql_observer_rejects_projection_and_tautology confirms assert_selected rejects a projection (identity column omitted) and a tautology (WHERE ?=? returning all rows with mismatched keys).

The acquisition regression exercises the real WarehouseSessionManager open path over an owned synthetic DuckDB file by injecting at connect_with_lock_retry; it asserts exactly one qualifying factory call, manager.mode is None before and after, valid exact reads on both sides, and manager.stop() cleanup.

Error distinctions are safe: duckdb.IOException becomes AttentionRecordUnavailableError with the synthetic marker absent from str(); WarehouseBusyError and RuntimeError propagate with identical object identity (caught is failure), rejecting any over-broad except Exception conversion.

Source authority holds: PUBLISHED with no publication store raises unavailable and never touches the warehouse (forbid_warehouse returns []); PREFER_PUBLISHED falls back to the warehouse; published-only display mutations make PG groups differ from warehouse while keys remain identical.

Identity and error correctness covered: empty textual identity mutations (charge_id, transaction_id, contract_id, reason) are admitted by the row models and Postgres store; the forged key never resolves; a canonical-looking unknown is not-found before invalidation then unavailable after; intact siblings remain exact; charge_id NULL and DROP COLUMN and DROP TABLE all yield unavailable.

No mutation and no annotation escapes: get_open_attention_items and all four source marts are byte-identical before and after reads; the file contains no skip/xfail/noqa/type-ignore; slow tests fail (not skip) when Docker is absent via the required_postgres assert.

Complete groups and both required selectors: all four kinds (anomaly/contract_review/contract_renewal/upcoming_cost) are exercised with whole-group equality, wrong/excluded IDs, true source SQL filtering, and no-warehouse-read observation; both the ordinary (not-slow) and explicit integration-and-slow selectors remain mandatory.

uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -m 'integration and slow' tests/test_attention_source_records.py
